findings.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/user.js.es6:209 — website_name is now server-computed but save() only copies bio_excerpt back from the PUT response, so after editing website in preferences the profile shows a stale/empty website_name until full reload (previously it was derived live from model.website).

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 — include_website_name lacks the trailing `?` that AMS (and every other include_ method in this serializer) uses, so it never gates inclusion and website_name is always emitted (null when no website), drifting the response shape from the stated intent.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/user.js.es6:17 — The public websiteName controller property is removed without deprecation, silently breaking any plugin/theme template or connector that reads websiteName on the user controller.

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 — include_website_name` lacks the `?` suffix so AMS never calls it, and website_name is not in untrusted_attributes, so a TL0 user's website domain/path leaks to anonymous viewers even though `website` itself is hidden by `include_website?` restrict_user_fields gating.

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:138 — URI(website)` raises InvalidURIError for IDN/non-ASCII hosts or paths with spaces and scheme-less values give host nil, so website_name becomes nil and the template (now gated on model.website_name) hides the website entirely where the old split('/')[2] still showed it.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user/user.hbs:66 — website_name is now a static server value that User#save never refreshes (only bio_excerpt is copied back), so after editing or clearing the website in preferences the profile shows the stale old name, even linking it with an empty href when the website was cleared.

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:146 — The equal-label-count heuristic compares everything after the first label, so unrelated hosts on a shared public suffix (e.g. foo.co.uk vs forum.co.uk, alice.github.io vs forum.github.io) are treated as the same site and get the full path shown.

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:141 — Host comparisons are case-sensitive (URI keeps "Example.COM" as-is) and the else branch only matches when the website is a parent of the instance, so same-site URLs like http://Example.com/u or www.example.com when the instance is example.com fall back to host-only display.

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:143 — Using `.host` drops the port that the old split('/')[2] kept, and appending `.path` turns a root URL like http://example.com/ into "example.com/" with a trailing slash.

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:43 — website_name is not in untrusted_attributes, and include_website_name lacks the trailing `?` so it never runs; restrict_user_fields? hides website from anonymous viewers of TL0 users, but website_name (its host and path) still leaks and is rendered by user.hbs, which undoes the anti-spam restriction

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:144 — The same-domain heuristic compares labels without checking the public suffix list, so on shared parent domains (e.g. forum.herokuapp.com, x.co.uk) an unrelated tenant's host counts as same-domain and its full user-controlled path is shown

spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:11 — TL0-anonymous spec's untrusted_attributes list was not extended with website_name, so the leak of website_name (with full path) for restricted users is not caught by tests.

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 — include_website_name lacks the trailing `?` so it is never used by AMS as a gate, and there is no spec asserting website_name is omitted when website is blank/restricted.
app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:146 — The equal-length sibling-subdomain branch (www.example.com vs forum.example.com, match and non-match) has zero test coverage.

spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:76 — No specs for nil/blank website, unparseable URL (rescue path), or scheme-less website like "example.com" (host nil, so the website is hidden entirely in the profile).

spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:88 — No negative test for a non-matching suffix (e.g. website ample.com or other.com vs forums.example.com) to prove the ends_with?("." + host) check doesn't over-match.

spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:76 — Edge cases such as mixed-case hosts, trailing slash, query strings, or ports on same-domain URLs are untested, leaving the rendered path format unspecified.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user/user.hbs:66 — Template now depends on server-provided model.website_name with no JS/acceptance test or fixture update to cover website rendering in the user profile.

goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/user.js.es6:209 — website_name is now server-computed but save() only copies bio_excerpt back from the PUT response, so after editing website in preferences the profile shows a stale/empty website_name until full reload (previously it was derived live from model.website).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does move website display from a client-side computed `websiteName` to server-provided `model.website_name` (controller removal + template change + serializer adds `website_name`). However, the finding’s core claim—`save()` only copying `bio_excerpt` back from the PUT response so `website_name` stays stale after editing—is not verifiable from the provided diff (no changes or context around `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/user.js.es6` save/update behavior are shown). From the diff alone we can’t confirm that updates omit `website_name` or that the client fails to update it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 — include_website_name lacks the trailing `?` that AMS (and every other include_ method in this serializer) uses, so it never gates inclusion and website_name is always emitted (null when no website), drifting the response shape from the stated intent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `:website_name` to the serializer’s emitted attributes and defines `def include_website_name` (no trailing `?`). In ActiveModel::Serializer, conditional inclusion hooks are conventionally `include_<attr>?`; with the method named without `?`, it won’t be invoked to gate the attribute, so `website_name` will be serialized unconditionally (often as `null` when `website` is blank), changing the response shape versus the apparent intent (`website.present?`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/user.js.es6:17 — The public websiteName controller property is removed without deprecation, silently breaking any plugin/theme template or connector that reads websiteName on the user controller.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `websiteName` computed property from `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/user.js.es6` and updates the core template to use `model.website_name` instead. This is an API/compatibility change at the controller level; while core is updated, the diff provides no deprecation alias/backwards-compat shim for `websiteName`, so any external plugin/theme code that referenced `websiteName` on the user controller would break. The existence of such external usage can’t be verified from the diff alone, so it’s a compatibility concern rather than a provable core defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 — include_website_name` lacks the `?` suffix so AMS never calls it, and website_name is not in untrusted_attributes, so a TL0 user's website domain/path leaks to anonymous viewers even though `website` itself is hidden by `include_website?` restrict_user_fields gating.

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb` the conditional inclusion hook is defined as `def include_website_name` (no `?`). In AMS/Discourse serializer patterns, the hook is `include_<attr>?`; without the `?` it won’t be invoked, making the gating ineffective/dead code. However, the finding’s claim that `website_name` is not in `untrusted_attributes` is contradicted by the diff: `:website_name` is explicitly added there.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:138 — URI(website)` raises InvalidURIError for IDN/non-ASCII hosts or paths with spaces and scheme-less values give host nil, so website_name becomes nil and the template (now gated on model.website_name) hides the website entirely where the old split('/')[2] still showed it.

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb`, `website_name` is derived from `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` and immediately `return`s if `website_host` is nil. However, `include_website_name` only checks `website.present?`, so the JSON can contain `website` but `website_name` be nil. The template was changed to render the website block only when `model.website_name` is present (`{{#if model.website_name}}`), meaning certain non-empty `website` values that fail URI parsing or yield no host will now be hidden entirely. The finding’s examples (InvalidURIError for spaces/IDN, schemeless URLs yielding host nil) are plausible given the diff, though input constraints aren’t shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user/user.hbs:66 — website_name is now a static server value that User#save never refreshes (only bio_excerpt is copied back), so after editing or clearing the website in preferences the profile shows the stale old name, even linking it with an empty href when the website was cleared.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `websiteName` computed property removed and the template now reads `model.website_name` from `UserSerializer#website_name` (conditionally included when `website.present?`). However, the finding’s core claim depends on client-side save/refresh behavior ("User#save never refreshes", "only bio_excerpt is copied back") that is not present in this diff, so the purported stale `website_name`/empty-href scenario cannot be verified from the shown changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:146 — The equal-label-count heuristic compares everything after the first label, so unrelated hosts on a shared public suffix (e.g. foo.co.uk vs forum.co.uk, alice.github.io vs forum.github.io) are treated as the same site and get the full path shown.

adjudication.rationale: In `website_name`, the branch `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` compares `website_host.split('.')[1..-1]` to `discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1]`. This treats any two hosts with the same number of labels and the same tail labels as “same site”, so `foo.co.uk` vs `forum.co.uk` (tail `co.uk`) and `alice.github.io` vs `forum.github.io` (tail `github.io`) will incorrectly match and return `website_host + URI(...).path`, exposing/showing the full path for unrelated hosts. That matches the finding and is a real behavioral defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:141 — Host comparisons are case-sensitive (URI keeps "Example.COM" as-is) and the else branch only matches when the website is a parent of the instance, so same-site URLs like http://Example.com/u or www.example.com when the instance is example.com fall back to host-only display.

adjudication.rationale: In `website_name`, the logic compares `website_host` to `Discourse.current_hostname` using exact string equality and suffix checks (`==`, `ends_with?`) without any explicit normalization (e.g., downcasing or stripping common subdomains). From the diff alone, cases like `website_host = "www.example.com"` and `discourse_host = "example.com"` will not match the `==` branch, won’t enter the `elsif` (since `discourse_host.split('.').length` is 2, not `> 2`), and will fail the `ends_with?("." << website_host)` check, resulting in returning just `website_host` (no path). That’s a real, diff-grounded edge-case/incompleteness in the new display logic, but the diff doesn’t prove it violates an explicit requirement, so it’s better treated as a non-bug review concern. The claim about URI host case preservation can’t be verified from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:143 — Using `.host` drops the port that the old split('/')[2] kept, and appending `.path` turns a root URL like http://example.com/ into "example.com/" with a trailing slash.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the old UI-derived `websiteName` used `website.split("/")[2]`, which would preserve a host+port string like `example.com:3000`. The new serializer computes `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host`, which omits any explicit port. That’s a concrete loss of information in `website_name` for URLs with non-default ports. Also, in branches where it returns `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`, a root URL with a trailing slash (`http://example.com/`) will yield a `path` of `/` and thus `example.com/`, whereas the previous split-based display would have been just `example.com`—a verifiable behavior change introduced by the new logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:43 — website_name is not in untrusted_attributes, and include_website_name lacks the trailing `?` so it never runs; restrict_user_fields? hides website from anonymous viewers of TL0 users, but website_name (its host and path) still leaks and is rendered by user.hbs, which undoes the anti-spam restriction

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` in `user_serializer.rb`, so the claim that it is not included there is false. Also, the newly added spec asserts `json[:website_name]` is present and equals expected values, which would fail if `include_website_name` “never runs”; therefore that part of the finding is not supported by the diff. The broader claim about `restrict_user_fields?` hiding `website` but leaking `website_name` cannot be verified from this diff alone and is contradicted by the `untrusted_attributes` change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:144 — The same-domain heuristic compares labels without checking the public suffix list, so on shared parent domains (e.g. forum.herokuapp.com, x.co.uk) an unrelated tenant's host counts as same-domain and its full user-controlled path is shown

adjudication.rationale: In `website_name`, the branch `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` treats two hosts as “same-domain” if all labels except the leftmost match (e.g., `x.herokuapp.com` vs `forum.herokuapp.com` both reduce to `herokuapp.com`), and then returns `website_host + URI(website).path`. This can incorrectly classify unrelated tenants on shared parent domains as same-domain and expose the full user-controlled path (vs just the host), matching the finding. The diff also adds tests for `forums.example.com`/`example.com` but none for shared-hosting/public-suffix edge cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:11 — TL0-anonymous spec's untrusted_attributes list was not extended with website_name, so the leak of website_name (with full path) for restricted users is not caught by tests.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly extends the serializer’s `untrusted_attributes` list to include `:website_name` (`app/serializers/user_serializer.rb` adds `:website_name` right after `:website`). Therefore the claim that the untrusted list “was not extended with website_name” is contradicted by the shown changes, and the alleged leak due to missing coverage doesn’t follow from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 — include_website_name lacks the trailing `?` so it is never used by AMS as a gate, and there is no spec asserting website_name is omitted when website is blank/restricted.

adjudication.rationale: The serializer adds `:website_name` to the attributes list and defines `include_website_name` (no trailing `?`). In AMS/Discourse serializer conventions, conditional inclusion hooks are named `include_<attr>?`, so as written this method likely won’t be called and won’t gate the `website_name` attribute. The diff also adds specs only for present `website`, not for omission when `website` is blank, so the intended gating behavior isn’t covered.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:146 — The equal-length sibling-subdomain branch (www.example.com vs forum.example.com, match and non-match) has zero test coverage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial branching logic in `UserSerializer#website_name`, including an `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` branch intended for sibling subdomains (e.g., `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`). The accompanying spec additions cover: different domains (`discourse.org` vs `example.com`), exact same domain (`example.com`), and instance domain being a subdomain of the website domain (`forums.example.com` vs `example.com`). No test sets both hosts to equal-length sibling subdomains to exercise the new `elsif` branch (both match and non-match cases), so that branch currently has no direct test coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:76 — No specs for nil/blank website, unparseable URL (rescue path), or scheme-less website like "example.com" (host nil, so the website is hidden entirely in the profile).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial parsing/normalization in `UserSerializer#website_name` using `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` plus conditional path-appending logic, and the template now gates display on `model.website_name`. The added specs only cover a well-formed `http://example.com/user` case and hostname comparisons; they do not cover edge inputs implied by the new implementation (blank/nil `website`, unparsable URLs triggering the `rescue nil`, or scheme-less values where `URI(...).host` can be nil). That’s a concrete, diff-grounded test gap rather than a proven defect in this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:88 — No negative test for a non-matching suffix (e.g. website ample.com or other.com vs forums.example.com) to prove the ends_with?("." + host) check doesn't over-match.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces nontrivial branching logic in `UserSerializer#website_name`, including a suffix check `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` (e.g., `forums.example.com` vs `example.com`). The added spec covers same-domain and parent-domain cases, but does not include a negative case where the website host is a similar but non-matching suffix (e.g. `ample.com` or `other.com` vs `forums.example.com`) to exercise the false branch and ensure the suffix logic doesn’t accidentally treat near-matches as parents. This is a concrete test coverage gap tied to the new logic, not a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:76 — Edge cases such as mixed-case hosts, trailing slash, query strings, or ports on same-domain URLs are untested, leaving the rendered path format unspecified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces nontrivial URL parsing/normalization logic in `UserSerializer#website_name` using `URI(website.to_s).host` and `URI(...).path`, plus string comparisons against `Discourse.current_hostname` (including `.split('.')` and `.ends_with?`). The added specs only cover simple lowercase host + path cases and do not cover edge inputs like mixed-case hosts (host comparisons are case-sensitive as written), trailing slashes, query strings/fragments, or ports, so the output format for these cases is indeed unspecified by tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user/user.hbs:66 — Template now depends on server-provided model.website_name with no JS/acceptance test or fixture update to cover website rendering in the user profile.

adjudication.rationale: The template was updated to use `model.website_name`, but this PR also adds `website_name` to `UserSerializer` (`:website_name`, `website_name`, `include_website_name`) and adds serializer specs covering the new field and its behavior (`spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb`). The finding’s claim that there is “no … test … update to cover website rendering” is contradicted at least in part by the added serializer tests, and the diff provides no evidence about missing JS/acceptance tests or fixture updates.
